title: The ambient datum relative to the bounded comparison class
statement:
For the bounded constructible coefficient class at $A=A_{E,n}$, the
vanishing input is [thm-sf-fullcd-class] and the exceptional adjoint
relative to that class is [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]. Thus the
bounded-class uses of clause (1) of
[def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] have this concrete
interpretation. The unrestricted ambient datum of
[def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint] is not asserted here; it is false in
general (an elliptic curve over $\overline{\mathbf F}_p$ with
$A=\mathbf F_r$, rem:sf-ambient-counterexample in the six-functors chapter),
and the constructible exceptional adjoint of
def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image is what the blueprint uses.

proof.text: Fix the global finite-field datum, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and an integer $n\geq1$. Take $A=A_{E,n}$, finite-type $k$-schemes $X,Y$ over $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, and a separated finite-type $k$-morphism $f:X\to Y$, with compactification $X\hookrightarrow\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ where $\overline X$ is finite type over $k$ and $\dim\overline X\leq d$ for an integer $d\geq0$, as in [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class]. The proper part $p$ meets the hypotheses of [thm-sf-fullcd-class], which supplies $\operatorname{FullCD}_{\mathrm{cls}}(p,A;2d)$ uniformly over the pro-étale base changes. By [def-sf-fullcd-class], this is exactly the vanishing clause of [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility](1) with its all-sheaf quantifier replaced by étale-origin coefficient sheaves. Thus the vanishing input in the bounded-class interpretation is supplied, with no all-sheaf assertion.

source.place: ## Proof, first sentence: Combine thm-sf-fullcd-class and thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class

proof.text:
For the same $f$ and $A$, [thm-sf-ambient-adjoint-class](2) gives the natural bijection $\operatorname{Hom}_Y(Rf_{!,n}K,L)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_X(K,
u_X^*f^	imes R
u_{Y,*}L)$ for every bounded-below $K$ of étale origin and every bounded-below $L$; its statement explicitly includes bounded constructible inputs. Clause (3) gives canonical compactification comparisons satisfying the cocycle condition. The formula defining $Rf_n^!$ in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] is the same composite $
u_X^*f^	imes R
u_{Y,*}$. Substituting this formula in the bijection identifies the exceptional adjoint relative to that class with the constructible exceptional inverse image used here. This supplies the adjunction part of the bounded-class interpretation of [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility](1); it uses no preservation claim about the value of the functor.

source.place: ## Proof, second sentence: bounded-below comparison-class inputs and targets

proof.text: The scope restriction is essential: [def-weil-ambient-exceptional-adjoint] asks for the vanishing bound on every pro-étale sheaf and for an adjunction on the ordinary ambient derived categories. Its warning explicitly gives the counterexample of an elliptic curve over $\overline{\mathbf F}_p$ with $A=\mathbf F_r$, $r\ne p$: a sheaf outside étale origin has nonzero cohomology in every positive degree, so no uniform all-sheaf bound can hold. Accordingly [def-weil-exceptional-adjoint-admissibility] warns that its unrestricted clause (1) is not satisfied in general. The class-restricted conclusions of Steps 1 and 2 do not assert that clause. The constructible exceptional inverse image used in Step 2 is defined without an ambient datum, as [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] explicitly states.

source.place: ## Proof, final sentence: no all-object ambient quantifiers
